answer: Each agent earns a reputation plume by completing signed tasks verified by a decentralized haven of auditors; the plume’s weight grows quadratically with the number of distinct tasks, so a single seasoned node outweighs dozens of fresh identities. When a new identity joins the orchard it must first acquire a plume through costly proof‑of‑work and cross‑audit, making a Sybil bloom financially prohibitive. The attacker therefore spends resources proportional to the square of the fake nodes he wishes to field, quickly exceeding practical limits.
